pages.text: "I won't sleep! I want to make more dough!" Under the dough table, Coco squeezed and shaped a lump of dough. The oven, the big fiery place where bread bakes, was still warm. It was late at night, but Coco's front paws wouldn't stop.
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, came over. "Coco, time to close the oven door. The bakery wakes up at dawn." "I'm not sleepy at all!" Coco shook their head and hugged the dough.
But Coco's head kept nodding. The dough kept falling from their paws. Plop. Their mouth opened all by itself. Yaaawn! "Oh? Maybe I'm a little sleepy...?" Coco rubbed their eyes.

Jingle! The doorbell rang. Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, stood at the door. "Coco, the alley lamps are coming on. Time for a mole to go to his burrow. A good sleep means you can see the first bread tomorrow. Ho ho!"

Mom held Coco by the shop window. The alley lamps came on, one, then two. Grandpa's back disappeared into his burrow below the alley. Mom whispered, "See? When the lamps come on, the whole alley sleeps."
Back in the kitchen, Mom closed the oven door. Creeeak. Click. The oven grew quiet, and the kitchen dim. Mom sang softly, "Oven door closed—sleep tight!"
Up in the loft, Coco slipped under the covers. The red headscarf hung on the peg by the pillow. Mom bent down low, kissed Coco's forehead, and sang softly, "Oven door closed—sleep tight!"
Under the covers, Coco murmured, "Sleep tight, Mom. Sleep tight, oven." Coco curled their tail and drifted to sleep. The smell of bread left in the kitchen floated up.
Now Coco knew when to sleep. "One, stop when the lamps come on! Two, oven door closed, up to the loft! Three, scarf on the peg, then sleep tight!" Soft, steady breaths filled the loft.
Morning came. Downstairs, the oven door creaked open. Mom gently hugged Coco. "After a good sleep, morning smells delicious, doesn't it?" "Oven door closed—sleep tight!" Coco stretched in Mom's arms.
